subject.title: fix: sleep tool — session-targeted wake, correct sandbox policy, doc fixes

question: Should OpenClaw add `sleep` as a second built-in delayed-follow-up API, or keep one-shot session-targeted cron as the canonical mechanism?
rationale: The repository already has a capable scheduling surface, while the proposed convenience wrapper changes the core model API and security boundary; code review cannot choose that permanent product contract.

options.title: Keep cron canonical
options.body: Close or substantially rework this PR and improve cron descriptions or helper UX instead of introducing a competing built-in tool.

options.title: Sponsor native sleep
options.body: Approve a distinct ephemeral timer primitive, but require embedded-runtime support, cancellation, restart semantics, owner/policy enforcement, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Accept cron wrapper
options.body: Intentionally expose a convenience wrapper over persisted cron and document its durability, authorization, and upgrade behavior as part of the core contract.

recommendation.title: Keep cron canonical
recommendation.body: Close or substantially rework this PR and improve cron descriptions or helper UX instead of introducing a competing built-in tool.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a core product/API direction choice rather than a mechanical implementation decision.
